title: Inner proof of a joined circuit proof
statement: Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits and $g$ ordered gates, and set $m=1+n+g$. Given an extension assignment $e\colon\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,1\}$ and an inner-proof assignment $q\colon\{1,\ldots,2^m+2^{m^2}\}\to\{0,1\}$, form a proof of length $m+2^m+2^{m^2}$ by placing $e$ in its first $m$ positions and $q$ in the remaining positions. Restricting this joined proof to those remaining positions recovers $q$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits and a finite ordered list of gates

An inner-proof assignment on $2^{1+n+g}+2^{(1+n+g)^2}$ Boolean coordinates
